narrative_markdown:
## Today's Forecast

A warm day is already on track with a high of 30°C (87°F) expected. The sky will shift from early Partly cloudy to midday Mostly clear, then become Mostly cloudy this evening. thunder possible, peaking this evening. The wind will be north-northeasterly overnight, turning southwest by midday, with a peak gust of 36 km/h (19 kt) ashore. UV will climb to a peak index of 9.3 today. Air quality is dominated by Dunga Beach reporting AQI 40, the highest of the three stations. As of 06:01, reports through 03:00: no rain; no thunder; high so far 23°C / 73°F; low so far 22°C / 72°F; peak sustained 7 km/h; sky partly cloudy.

## Extended Outlook

NEXT THREE DAYS show temperatures and winds much the same through Saturday, with showers and thunderstorms likely each day. Thursday Mostly cloudy, Friday Mostly cloudy, Saturday Mostly cloudy, Sunday Mostly cloudy, Monday Partly cloudy, Tuesday Partly cloudy, Wednesday Partly cloudy. Models agree that Thursday will be wet with 4 of 4 models calling rain, and Friday the same. Saturday (Day+3) is also 4 of 4 models wet, with rain amounts between 5.1 and 13.8 mm and a high ranging from 28 to 30°C. The call’s Day+3 forecast matches this spread. The Day+7 call also predicts rain, 80% chance, with a high near 27–29°C. RECORD: Day+3 best rain record Best Match, right 80% of the last 30 checks.

## Severe Weather / Hazard Potential

The CAPE values peak at 3540 J/kg in the UKMO model, well above the thunderstorm threshold, indicating a risk of strong downdrafts and sudden gusts that could exceed the forecast wind of 36 km/h (19 kt). No official KMD severe weather bulletin has been issued for today, so no formal warning is in force.

## Winam Gulf — Conditions for Boaters

The Winam Gulf wind will be northeasterly overnight at 5 km/h (3 kt) gusting 9 km/h (5 kt), then shift to south-southwesterly by midday at 9 km/h (5 kt) gusting 19 km/h (10 kt), and continue into the evening at 12 km/h (7 kt) gusting 19 km/h (10 kt); peak gust reaches 27 km/h (15 kt). Because thunder is possible this evening, gusts could briefly surge above these values during a storm.

## Detailed Discussion

### Synoptic Overview

Across roughly 2,600 km, pressure is lowest toward the north (1010 hPa) and highest toward the northeast (1014 hPa) — a 4 hPa spread, a moderate large-scale gradient. The lower pressure to the north is deepening over the next three days. Pressure is also falling toward the northwest — a large-scale feature building in that direction. Pressure overhead is near-steady. BASIN PRESSURE: across 5 points, today's mean sea-level pressure sits between 1013.1 and 1015.4 hPa; near-steady over three days (+0.5 hPa). The call notes a pressure trend of +0.1 hPa and a moderate large-scale gradient with the lowest pressure toward the north.

### Forecaster Confidence Notes

REVIEW notes that at Day+0 no model is meaningfully better than the others, reflecting a settled picture despite uneven KMD coverage. RECORD shows Best Match holds the Day+0 rain record, yet the call’s peak gust of 36 km/h (19 kt) is higher than Best Match’s 38.5 km/h forecast, indicating the model slightly under-forecast peak wind. The call’s high of 30°C aligns with the ECMWF and GFS ranges but exceeds ECMWF’s slight under-forecast of daytime highs. KMD forecasts a maximum of 29°C, modestly lower than the call, suggesting a slight divergence. DATA SUFFICIENCY reports 57 checks for Day+0, providing a solid basis, though KMD’s fewer observations limit direct comparison. Overall confidence is moderate, with model spread narrow and observations supporting the call’s key elements.

Further out, temperatures and winds much the same through Wednesday, with showers and thunderstorms likely Sunday and Monday, showers and thunderstorms possible Tuesday, and dry Wednesday with thunderstorms possible. Sunday: all four models wet, highs around 29 °C. Monday: all four models wet, highs around 28 °C. Tuesday: all three models that reach it wet, highs around 29 °C, thunder possible rather than likely.

Only GFS, ECMWF and ICON reach past Monday. ICON is the wetter solution from Sunday to Monday; GFS, ECMWF and UKMO keep it drier. Wednesday's call: rain, 80%, with one of two models wet; highs around 28 °C. At this lead ECMWF has the best record, right 77% of the time over 70 checks.
